easy.q: To whom does the father speak at the beginning?

easy.explanation: He tells his son to receive his words and hide his commandments with him.
easy.q: What does the father tell his son to do with his commandments?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “For the LORD giveth wisdom.”
easy.q: Who gives wisdom according to these verses?

answers: As seeking silver and hidden treasures
medium.explanation: The seeker is told to seek wisdom as silver and search for it as hidden treasures.
medium.q: How is the search for wisdom described?

medium.explanation: The phrase means to keep the commandments close and preserve them.
medium.q: What does “hide my commandments with thee” mean in context?

medium.explanation: The passage connects listening, crying for knowledge, and seeking wisdom with understanding.
medium.q: What leads to understanding the fear of the LORD and finding knowledge?

answers: Receiving and keeping wisdom, seeking it, then understanding
Searching for silver, abandoning wisdom, then gaining knowledge
challenge.explanation: The verses move from receiving and keeping wisdom to seeking it and then understanding.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the process in these verses?

answers: A person seeks wisdom, and the LORD gives wisdom and understanding
A person receives everything without asking
The LORD gives wisdom only to those who refuse to listen
challenge.explanation: The person must seek and listen, but the LORD is the one who gives wisdom.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between human effort and the gift of wisdom?

challenge.explanation: Searching for treasure suggests determined and sustained effort.
challenge.q: What quality of the search is emphasized by comparing it with silver and hidden treasures?

answers: Those who leave the right way
easy.explanation: Verse 7 calls the LORD “a buckler to them that walk uprightly.”
The verse says, “He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous.”
easy.q: What does the LORD lay up for the righteous?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “When wisdom entereth into thine heart.”

answers: The paths of judgment and the way of his saints
medium.explanation: He keeps the paths of judgment and preserves the way of his saints.
medium.q: What does the LORD keep according to verse 8?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to reliable wisdom that benefits the righteous.
medium.q: What does “sound wisdom” mean in this context?

answers: They cause a person to leave judgment
medium.explanation: Knowledge becomes pleasant to the soul, and understanding preserves the person.
medium.q: What is the result when wisdom and knowledge enter the heart?

answers: Those who walk uprightly receive his protection
Uprightness removes the need for wisdom
Uprightness leads to paths of darkness
challenge.explanation: The LORD is a buckler to those who walk uprightly.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage show between uprightness and the LORD’s protection?

answers: It gives understanding and also protects
It is only an outward treasure
It leads people away from the right path
challenge.explanation: Wisdom helps a person understand righteousness and preserves him from danger.
challenge.q: How does the role of wisdom develop in this passage?

answers: It enters the heart and protects the person’s way
It works only among the wicked
challenge.explanation: Wisdom enters the heart, while understanding and discretion preserve the person’s path.
challenge.q: Why can wisdom be said to work both inwardly and outwardly?

paragraphs.title: Rescue from Evil Ways and Seduction

answers: The way of the evil man
easy.explanation: The passage says it is “To deliver thee from the way of the evil man.”
easy.q: What does understanding deliver a person from?

easy.explanation: Verse 16 describes the strange woman as one who flatters with her words.
Verse 18 says, “For her house inclineth unto death.”
easy.q: Where does the strange woman’s house incline?

answers: They leave upright paths and rejoice in evil
They keep the paths of the righteous
medium.explanation: They leave the paths of uprightness, walk in darkness, and rejoice to do evil.
medium.q: What do the evil people in these verses do?

answers: Her words are smooth and seductive
Her words are difficult to understand
medium.explanation: To flatter with words is to use pleasant or persuasive speech to entice someone.
medium.q: What does it mean that the strange woman flatters with her words?

answers: Leaving uprightness leads them into evil ways
Leaving uprightness returns them to the good path
medium.explanation: The passage describes people who abandon uprightness and then delight in evil.
medium.q: What is the relationship between leaving uprightness and rejoicing in evil?

answers: Evil men and a flattering strange woman
challenge.explanation: Understanding delivers a person from both evil men and the strange woman.
challenge.q: What two main dangers appear in this passage?

answers: Both turn a person away from the paths of life
Both lead to the paths of the righteous
Both are based on keeping uprightness
challenge.explanation: The first way leads into darkness, and the second leads to death and does not return to life.
challenge.q: What do the way of evil men and the way of the strange woman have in common?

answers: Her way is a grave danger from which return is difficult
Her way safely leads to life
challenge.explanation: The statement presents her path as a serious danger that separates people from the paths of life.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “None that go unto her return again”?

paragraphs.title: The Way of the Good and the Fate of the Wicked

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “That thou mayest walk in the way of good men.”
easy.q: In which way should a person walk?

easy.explanation: Verse 21 says, “For the upright shall dwell in the land.”
easy.q: Who shall dwell in the land?

answers: They will be cut off and rooted out
They will remain in the land forever
easy.explanation: Verse 22 says they shall be cut off from the earth and rooted out of it.
easy.q: What will happen to the wicked and transgressors?

medium.explanation: The verse says to keep the paths of the righteous.
medium.q: What should a person keep according to verse 20?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes being removed or uprooted from the earth.
medium.q: What does “rooted out of it” mean?

answers: The upright remain in the land, while the wicked are removed
The upright are removed, while the wicked remain
Both the upright and wicked remain
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts the dwelling of the upright with the removal of the wicked.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in the final two verses?

answers: Wisdom leads a person to walk with good men and keep righteous paths
They cancel the need for wisdom
challenge.explanation: The conclusion shows that wisdom directs a person toward good men and righteous paths.
challenge.q: How do verses 20–22 explain the purpose of the previous instruction?

answers: The upright and perfect remain in it
The land is for those who leave uprightness
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 connects remaining in the land with being upright and perfect.
challenge.q: What connection is made between remaining in the land and a person’s character?

answers: A person’s chosen way is connected with his fate
A person’s choice of way has no importance
Wickedness and uprightness lead to the same result
challenge.explanation: The upright remain in the land, while the wicked and transgressors are removed.
challenge.q: What moral conclusion comes from the contrast between verses 21 and 22?
